text:
Connecting people looking for a home
with people who have one to rent
A shared place to find and offer rentals
RentBridge is a full-stack rental marketplace for customers and property owners.
Browse and filter rooms, apartments, houses and PG listings.
Publish listings, add photos, and manage their own properties.
Both sides can move from discovery to a structured contact request, with notifications when the owner responds.
Sources: README.md; frontend/src/main.jsx; backend/src/routes/properties.js; backend/src/routes/contactRequests.js; backend/src/routes/notifications.js
Rental discovery and first contact can be fragmented
The project addresses common friction in the rental search journey:
Renters may need to move between sources to compare available places.
Rent, type, location and photos can be presented inconsistently.
Finding a listing does not always provide a clear next step to reach its owner.
Sharing an exact address or personal contact details too early can be undesirable.
These points frame the product problem; they are not findings from a user study.
Sources: Problem framing inferred from the RentBridge product flows in README.md, frontend/src/main.jsx, and backend/src/routes/properties.js
Search listings by city or area, property type and maximum rent.
Let owners create, edit and remove their own property listings.
Send a contact request tied to a specific property.
Keep exact address and poster email out of public listing results.
Customers browse current listings and narrow results by location, type and budget.
Owners add property details and up to five supported photos, then manage their listings.
A customer requests contact. The owner accepts or declines; acceptance shares contact details.
A notification is created for the owner when a request arrives and for the customer after a decision.
Sources: frontend/src/main.jsx; backend/src/routes/properties.js; backend/src/routes/contactRequests.js; backend/src/routes/notifications.js; backend/src/models/Notification.js
A browser client backed by an API and document database
Search, listing forms, account flow, owner dashboard and notifications.
REST endpoints for auth, properties, contact requests and notifications.
User, Property, ContactRequest and Notification models.
Bearer-token authentication; passwords are hashed before storage.
Up to five JPG, PNG or WebP photos per listing; signature checks validate file content.
Sources: frontend/package.json; backend/package.json; backend/src/server.js; backend/src/routes/auth.js; backend/src/routes/properties.js; backend/src/models/User.js; backend/src/models/Property.js
Data flow: search, listing, and contact
Public listing responses hide exact addresses. On acceptance, the requester receives the poster’s email and address.

Sources: backend/src/server.js; backend/src/routes/properties.js; backend/src/routes/contactRequests.js; backend/src/routes/notifications.js; backend/src/models/Property.js; backend/src/models/ContactRequest.js; backend/src/models/Notification.js
What the implemented flows are designed to improve
Search and filters bring multiple listing types into one browsing flow.
A request on a listing gives the owner a way to respond before details are shared.
Owners can publish, edit and remove properties they own.
Notifications connect a request to an accept or decline decision.
Expected product benefits; this project includes no measured user outcomes.
Sources: Impact statements are expected outcomes inferred from frontend/src/main.jsx and backend/src/routes/properties.js, contactRequests.js, and notifications.js
Local photo storage • newest 100 listings • process-local rate limiting • no ratings or identity verification
Move listing photos to persistent or managed object storage.
Add pagination, richer filters and location-based search.
Explore verified profiles, reviews and stronger abuse controls.
Consider viewing schedules, applications and payment integrations.
